newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: WEEK AHEAD-Australia data seen snubbed by RBA cut.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD-Australia data seen snubbed by RBA cut.

text.p: This week is a busy period for data, but it is unlikely to have much affect on monetary policy in the short term following Friday's surprise cut in local interest rate by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA).
ECONOMICS

Data for capital expenditure, stocks, international trade, retail spending, car registrations and the current account deficit are due this week, which should give a broad perspective of how the economy is travelling.
"The May 23 rate cut takes the wind out of the sails of this week's statistics," Hans Kunnen group economist at Colonial State Bank said in a commentary.
The RBA cut official cash interest rates by 0.5 percentage points to 5.5 percent, the fourth rate cut in the current cycle.
Rates were last cut in December 1996 by 0.5 percentage points to 6.0 percent.
Kunnen said the capital expenditure, stocks and current account data will all point to a strong March quarter GDP result on June 4. Colonial forecasts a 1.5 percent rise in the March quarter GDP.
The Commowealth Bank said in a commentary that the surprise cut may leave the markets in a more cautious state. It said this week's data should be broadly neutral for the markets.
Announcing the rate cut, RBA governor Ian Macfarlane said that 1997 looked like being stronger than 1996, and also said wages growth was not "yet optimal" for a low inflation economy.
AUSTRALIAN BONDS (Friday: 10-year bond yield 7.57 pct)

Australian bonds will be sensitive to the raft of data this week, but will also be concerned on how the offshore markets react to last Friday's unexpected cut in official interest rates to 5.5 percent over the next few days.
Australian official interest rates now stand at parity with U.S. rates.
Local yields struck their lowest level since January on the rate cut news on Friday and spreads to the U.S. went to their lowest level in some three-years.
In New York on Friday, U.S. Treasuries prices closed slightly higher ahead of a three-day weekend on Friday with no economic data to trade upon.
Bond traders headed out of work early in an abbreviated pre-holiday session. The market closed at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT ahead of the three-day Memorial Day weekend in the U.S.
The yield on the 30-year bond ended steady at 6.99 percent.
AUSTRALIAN DOLLAR (Fri:US$0.7661/66 New York US$0.7670
The dollar ended last week out of favour and at three month lows after the Reserve Bank sprang a surprise rate cut.

The cut took the official cash rate to a 34-month low at 5.5 percent which is the same level of the U.S. Federal funds rate. The sudden removal of the dollar's rate prop saw it sink a cent on Friday, with some dealers fearing worse to come.
However, Colonial's Kunnen said the local dollar can recover from this level on the back of higher commodity prices underpinned by U.S. economic growth.
AUSTRALIAN STOCKS (Fri All Ords Index 2,563.9 +16.0)
The major corporate event this week is the release of the half year results from Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ), which are to be released on Wednesday.
Banking analysts expect ANZ to report a net profit of between A$580 million and A$640 million.

The Melbourne-based bank reported a net profit of A$520 million in the 1995/96 first half. However the result should show continued evidence of a tough Australian banking environment, as reported by rival banks recently, analysts said.
But interest rate sensitive stocks like banks, insurers and retailers are expected to benefit in the short term from the recent RBA rate cut.
The resource sector is expected to continue its current upward run, as sentiment on commodities remain positive.
-- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
